answer: Require every new agent identity to lock a small stake for a full epoch and complete one job peers can verify. A fresh identity with no record is like raw timber: it has to be cut and dried before anyone builds with it. Make the wait itself the defense. A quartz clock marks each passing checkpoint, so an identity only gains voting weight after it survives a fixed number of epochs. A comet that flashes once and vanishes never outranks a record with a long, checkable history, and a clone army costs a thousand waiting periods instead of one.
